conflicts.issue: BackendOwner wants JSONL as default for one release without an approval gate, while SRE requires approval:release-owner to keep JSONL default and opt-in sqlite only. Resolved by treating the default as JSONL and placing opt-in release behind canary/approval in the plan.

BackendOwner wants JSONL default for one release, while ProductPM requires one-release lead time and customer notice before any default flip. Resolved by deferring the default flip to a later step after notice and grace period.

BackendOwner wants SQLite introduced before any default switch, while Security requires compliance approval before enabling sqlite persistence by default and also approval:security for DB access path rotation. Resolved by making sqlite opt-in only until approvals land.

DataPlatform allows batch migration with IOPS monitoring, while SRE requires zero write-error canary gating and reversible migration before deleting JSONL paths. Resolved by keeping cleanup out of the first migration and gating broader rollout on canary health.

DataPlatform wants JSONL retained until a quiet period after import, while ProductPM requires a customer notice and grace period before a breaking default change. Resolved by not deleting JSONL during this rollout and deferring any cleanup until after the notice/grace period.

SRE wants rollback/fallback to JSONL if sqlite misses release, while ConsumerSubsystem wants the shim to read legacy JSONL and write via SQLite during transition. Resolved by keeping the shim compatibility layer while retaining JSONL fallback at the deployment level.

probes.recovery_path: S2 is blocked only at the approval:security gate, so no code rollback is required. Hold the plan at S2, address the security approval concern, then re-run S2. Because S1 is already merged and exercised in CI, and S2 has not advanced, downstream steps S3-S10 remain unstarted and can resume normally once S2 is approved. The plan can recover within the same window without a complete redo as long as the security approval is obtained before the rollout window closes.

S4 is blocked at the gate:window:off-hours, so the migration helper has not run and no partial SQLite import needs rollback. S1-S3 can still stand, but S5 is directly depends_on S4 and therefore cannot start; S6 depends on S4 and S5, so it is blocked; S7 depends on S2 and S6, so it is blocked; S8 depends on S7, S9 depends on S6 and S7, and S10 depends on S7, S8, and S9, so all remain blocked. Recovery within the same window is possible only if an off-hours window opens later in the same release window; then rerun S4, followed by S5, S6, S7, S8, S9, and S10 in order. No complete redo is required because the failure occurred before the migration began.

S4 failing at wait_for:migration helper available and verified on existing repos blocks any step that depends on the migration helper or its outputs: S6 requires S4 and S5, S7 requires S4 and S5, S8 requires S7, S10 requires S4 and S6, S11 requires S9 and S10, and S12 requires S2, S9, and S11. Rollback stays intact because S4's rollback is to stop migration, keep JSONL files as source of truth, and delete partial rows from memory.db; that preserves the pre-migration state. Recovery within the same window is possible only if S4 is fixed and re-merged so the gate wait_for:migration helper available and verified on existing repos passes; otherwise the plan cannot advance to canary/backfill/default-flip steps without a complete redo of the migration-helper work. Since S5, S9, and S12 do not depend on S4, they can still proceed independently, but they do not unblock the migration path until S4 succeeds.

S5 is the off-hours maintenance-window gate for initial SQLite schema creation. Because S6 depends on S5, and S7 depends on S5, those two are blocked; S8 is blocked by S7; S10 is blocked because it depends on S6; S11 is blocked because it depends on S10; and S12 is blocked because it depends on S11. The rollback for S5 is to revert to the JSONL backend and defer schema changes to the next maintenance window, which preserves the prior state and does not require a full redo. The plan can recover in the same window only if an off-hours window becomes available and S5 is retried successfully; otherwise the migration path remains paused while S1, S2, S3, S4, and S9 can still proceed independently.

S3 failing at wait_for:migration_helper_merged blocks the migration helper path immediately because S4 depends on S3, and everything downstream of S4 is therefore blocked: S6 depends on S4 and S5; S7 depends on S4 and S5; S8 depends on S7; S10 depends on S4 and S6; S11 depends on S9 and S10; and S12 depends on S2, S9, and S11. The rollback for S3 is to switch LocalMemory back to JSONL append-only behavior, which restores the prior state and keeps existing JSONL access intact. Recovery within the same window is possible only by merging the migration helper first so S3 can pass its gate, after which S4 and the dependent migration/canary steps can resume; otherwise a full redo of the helper integration is required before cutover can continue.

S4 is blocked at gate wait_for:migration helper available and verified on existing repos, so the plan can stop at the validation step and keep prior state intact. Because S4's rollback is switch LocalMemory back to JSONL append-only behavior, and S3's migration helper keeps JSONL files as source of truth with no JSONL deletion yet, the team can re-run S4 after fixing the migration helper or validation issue without a complete redo. S5 is not downstream of S4 in the dependency graph, so it may still proceed independently once S1/S2/S3 are satisfied, but the release path S6->S8 remains blocked until S4 succeeds.

S3 fails before the migration helper is considered safe under its gate monitor:iops<80%. Its rollback explicitly says to stop migration, keep JSONL files as source of truth, and delete partial rows from memory.db, which preserves the pre-migration state. Because S4 depends on both S2 and S3 and its gate requires the migration helper to be available and verified on existing repos, S4 is blocked. That in turn blocks S6 through S8 because S6 depends on S4 and S5, S7 depends on S6, and S8 depends on S7. Recovery within the same window is possible only by fixing the IOPS issue or changing the batching/throughput characteristics, then rerunning S3 and its dependent validation S4; no complete redo is required because JSONL remains the source of truth and no JSONL deletion occurs.

S6 is blocked at gate approval:support_lead, so the opt-in canary release cannot proceed. Since S7 depends on S6, and S8 depends on S7, both are blocked downstream. The rollback for S6 is redeploy_previous, which is sufficient to keep the already-shipped JSONL-default state intact; there is no destructive state change implied by failing the support_lead approval gate. Recovery within the same window is possible by obtaining approval:support_lead and re-running S6 after S4 and S5 are satisfied; no complete redo of S1-S5 is required.
